A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ADASAP research. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and can be matched across the formatting changes and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original regression benchmarks, large-scale taxi inference, Bayesian optimization experiments, and supplementary timing and GPU-scaling results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a synthetic tail-averaging study in Appendix C.6 and Figure 5.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 change the tail-average summation endpoint from t+1 to t while retaining the normalization 2/(t+1), aligning the pseudocode with Appendix B's averaging convention. The remaining SAP/ADASAP procedure is unchanged, and both versions' main experiments omit tail averaging.

E1.justification: Appendix C.6 adds a synthetic RBF kernel-regression scenario with 1,000 samples for studying subspace convergence. The six real-data regression benchmarks, taxi dataset, and synthetic Matérn Bayesian optimization tasks are retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark comparisons retain ADASAP-I, SDD-1, SDD-10, SDD-100, and PCG, including the same divergence and memory-failure exclusions. The new study toggles the existing tail-averaging option within the proposed method.

E3.justification: The new study evaluates normalized squared RKHS error over top-ell subspaces with ell = 10, 100, and 1000, sweeping blocksizes 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, and 500 against kernel-matrix passes. Existing benchmark splits, preprocessing, budgets, and metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.6 and Figure 5 add a focused ablation testing whether tail averaging improves convergence across blocksizes and spectral subspaces. The existing identity-preconditioner comparison, GPU-scaling study, and supplementary training-versus-test analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five benchmark splits with mean curves and best-to-worst bands, five Bayesian optimization seeds, and one taxi split. The new tail-averaging study supplies no additional repeat-count, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing information.

E6.justification: New Figure 5 reports benefits from averaging for ell = 10 at small blocksizes, no benefit for ell = 100 or 1000, and slower convergence at larger blocksizes. Tables 1–2 and the matched benchmark, taxi, GPU-scaling, and supplementary timing results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.2, Corollary 3.3, and Appendix B retain their formal assumptions, bounds, and proof arguments. The added A_lambda = A + lambda I shorthand and expanded explanations of the two convergence phases do not introduce new mathematical results.

C1.justification: Introduction contribution 2 now explicitly qualifies condition-number-free posterior estimation as reaching moderate accuracy and connects it to ADASAP's test-error performance. The main empirical-superiority, scalability, and Bayesian optimization claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly explains that moderate accuracy can suffice with noisy data, while high-accuracy convergence remains condition dependent. It interprets the new ablation as supporting omission of tail averaging, which can hurt performance at larger blocksizes. Both versions acknowledge the unresolved gap between SAP theory and practical ADASAP.

D1.justification: Table 1 newly documents the input dimensions of all six benchmarks. Appendix C.6 provides the synthetic experiment's kernel, sample size, error measure, and parameter sweep, although data-generation and repetition details remain unspecified. Existing implementation, hardware, software, preprocessing, and code-access information is retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A.2 expands the comparison with already-cited Rathore et al. (2025), distinguishing this work's exact, tail-averaged subspace analysis from approximate SAP's global convergence analysis and explaining the relevance to early test-error progress. The cited-work set is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized explanatory revisions, clarifies notation and terminology, adds numbered subsections 4.1.1–4.1.3, and introduces Appendix C.6. The overall section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts the NeurIPS format throughout, with a redesigned title and author block, narrower text area, removed running preprint headers, and widespread resizing and repositioning of figures and algorithms. It also adds six-panel Figure 5 and a feature-dimension row in Table 1; the former Figures 5–6 are retained as Figures 6–7.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies the accuracy limits of its theoretical contribution, corrects the averaging endpoint, and adds focused evidence supporting the practical omission of tail averaging. The expanded prior-work comparison and dataset dimensions also improve understanding. These are limited gains: the principal results and proofs remain unchanged, the new synthetic study lacks generation and repetition details, and the SAP-to-ADASAP theoretical gap remains unresolved.
